findings.title: Worker-cap test is tautological (does not exercise production constant)
findings.detail: test_backtest_batch_workers_capped re-implements min(8, os.cpu_count() or 4) locally and asserts on the local variable; it never reads _cfg.BACKTEST_BATCH_WORKERS (gpu_fuzzy_trader/config.py:387). A regression changing config.py:387 would not be caught. Production invariant holds by construction today. Recommend a subprocess check (mock os.cpu_count=2 before importing config, assert prints 2) when task-3 introduces resolve_backtest_workers(); not blocking task-1 since task-3 owns this logic and its gates.

findings.title: File mode 100644, not executable despite shebang
findings.detail: git ls-files -s shows 100644. All documented invocations use .venv/bin/python so no functional impact; set chmod +x in a follow-up for direct ./scripts/benchmark_t4.py execution.

findings.title: VRAM fallback window wider than spec and can misclassify named non-T4 16GiB GPUs
findings.detail: Fallback accepts 14.5-16.5 GiB vs spec '15-16 GiB', and applies even when gpu_name IS available but lacks 't4' (e.g. V100/RTX 4060 Ti 16GB -> is_t4=True). Also name substring 't4' matches NVIDIA T400/T600/T1000. Acceptable for task-1 log-only skeleton (plan sanctions vram-based detection); tighten in task-2 before is_t4_runtime gates any behavior change.

findings.title: --dry-run still runs micro-benchmarks unless --skip-micro-bench also passed
findings.detail: Dry-run writes nothing (correct), but runs JAX engine compile (~1s observed). Slightly surprising semantics; acceptance only requires JSON output at --dry-run, gate passes. run_data_loader_benchmark measures synthetic DataFrame construction rather than project Data_Loader (minor sketch deviation).
